set: English Drill 2: Vocabulary, idioms and usage

sections.name: English drill: Vocabulary, idioms and usage

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “prolific”:
questions.why: Prolific = producing much (work, fruit, offspring). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “meticulous”:
questions.why: Meticulous = showing great attention to detail. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “benevolent”:
questions.why: Benevolent = well-meaning and kind. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “transient”:
questions.why: Transient = lasting only a short time. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “impede”:
questions.why: Impede = hinder. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “frugal”:
questions.why: Frugal = sparing with money; opposite: extravagant. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “scarcity”:
questions.why: Opposite of scarcity is abundance (plenty). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “convergence”:
questions.why: GPSC asked this pair in 2023. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “artificial”:
questions.why: Static vocabulary. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “heed”:
questions.why: Heed = pay attention to. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “to bury the hatchet”:
questions.why: Bury the hatchet = end a quarrel. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “a blessing in disguise”:
opts: something that seems bad but turns out good
questions.why: Standard idiom. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “to let the cat out of the bag”:
questions.why: Standard idiom. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the meaning of the idiom “once in a blue moon”:
questions.why: Standard idiom. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “The doctor asked him to ______ smoking.”
questions.why: Give up = stop doing; give in = surrender. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “The officer promised to ______ the complaint.”
questions.why: Look into = investigate. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb: “It took her weeks to ______ the fever.”
questions.why: Get over = recover from (GPSC 2026). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the one word for: “a doctor who treats children”
questions.why: One-word substitution. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the one word for: “a disease that spreads over a whole country or the world”
questions.why: Epidemic = widespread in one community at a time; endemic = regularly found in an area. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the one word for: “a person who cannot be corrected”
questions.why: One-word substitution. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.why: Double c, double m. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.why: GPSC 2024 key: 'benefited' (single t). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the figure of speech: “The wind whispered through the trees.”
questions.why: Human action (whispering) given to the wind. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the figure of speech: “The child is the father of the man.”
questions.why: An apparently absurd statement that holds a truth (GPSC 2026). GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Identify the figure of speech: “He is as brave as a lion.”
questions.why: A comparison using 'as' or 'like'. GPSC-style practice item.
